name: Color Assembly
character: A contemporary quilt collective with vermilion, cobalt, oversized geometric cloth, bold sans typography, and a manifesto-led home page.

sections.heading: Different ways in. One very good room.

items.title: The open table
items.body: Bring the quilt that will not behave. We have spare pins and opinions, if you want them.

items.title: The color experiment
items.body: Try a palette you would normally put back. A small block is a good place to take a chance.

items.title: The wall
items.body: Finished is worth sharing. So is the interesting thing that happened on the way there.

sections.heading: Less scrolling. More sewing.
sections.note: A first quilt, a fifth attempt, a sketch on a napkin. Bring what you have.

sections.heading: Make this your own
sections.html: Sample text — replace me: Add your real venue, meeting format, and current challenge. The quilt image is illustrative sample artwork, not a claim about a member’s finished work.

sections.title: Your kind of people. Your kind of making.
sections.body: Come for a meeting. Stay for the ideas that happen when we sew together.

sections.title: There is no house style. There is a shared table.
sections.subtitle: {{guild_name}} is a place to try things in cloth, ask generous questions, and make work that feels like your own.

sections.heading: Curiosity is the entry requirement.
sections.html: Sample text — replace me: Tell visitors how your collective started and who hosts it. Explain your approach to modern quilting without making newcomers feel they need a design vocabulary.

items.title: Credit the idea
items.body: Name the pattern designer, teacher, maker, and quilter when you share work.

items.title: Ask before advising
items.body: Sometimes a quilt wants critique. Sometimes its maker just wants to show you.

items.title: Make room
items.body: Different budgets, bodies, schedules, and experience levels belong at the same table.

sections.title: Bring the idea you cannot leave alone.
sections.subtitle: Open sew days and small experiments that get you past the sketchbook.

items.title: Choose a gathering
items.body: Check the events calendar for times, venue details, and any guest registration.

items.title: Pack one project
items.body: Bring your usual tools. Each event lists whether you need a machine or hand-sewing kit.

items.title: Find a seat
items.body: Say hello to the host. There is no requirement to bring something finished.

sections.heading: A few things you might be wondering

items.q: Do I need to make modern quilts?
items.a: You need curiosity, not a portfolio. Traditional skills and unexpected fabrics both have a place here.

items.q: Can I join from outside the city?
items.a: Check the calendar for the format of each gathering. Contact us about any remote sessions before joining.
